result.title: ESG Assessment Framework: Overview and Considerations
result.summary: ILPA’s ESG Assessment Framework helps limited partners evaluate and benchmark general partners’ ESG integration, guide goal-setting discussions, and track progress. It groups practices into four stages: Not Present, Developing, Intermediate, and Advanced. The framework is representative, not exhaustive or a comprehensive best-practice guide; practices are evolving, and ILPA plans periodic updates based on feedback and questions. Developed with mid- and large-cap buyout managers in mind, it may offer a starting point for other private-market asset classes but was not designed for them. Assessments should account for managers’ size and resources, recognize that descriptions are directional rather than substitutes for local or regulatory requirements, and avoid assuming a one-size-fits-all approach. The framework supports analysis and dialogue with GPs.

result.title: Frequently Asked Questions
key_items: What market sizes are the Framework intended for? Can I use the Framework for other market sizes?
What asset class was this Framework created for? Can I use the Framework for other asset classes, including venture capital, real estate, infrastructure and private credit?
Why are Responsiveness to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion and Climate Risks and Opportunities broken out as separate sections?
Is it leading practice to invest only with GPs who rank in intermediate/leading categories?
What about situations where a GP invests but does not have a majority ownership stake in a portfolio company? Do the practices outlined in the framework still apply?
Can the ESG Assessment Framework be used in conjunction with the ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire?
Has ILPA considered assigning scores or grades to each category?
Where can I find additional resources pertaining to ESG?
I have identified a best practice that is not included in the framework or have a suggestion to update the Framework. Can I send these to ILPA for consideration?
result.summary: The FAQ explains that the ESG Framework targets mid-to-large-cap private equity buyout managers, but can be adapted to smaller managers and other private-market asset classes with appropriate context. DEI and climate are separate sections because they are strategic priorities requiring specific consideration. The Framework is not a requirement to invest only in advanced GPs; it supports assessment, dialogue, and tracking improvement. For minority investments, GPs may have limited influence or data access, so LPs should discuss their approach with them and majority investors. The Framework complements ILPA’s Due Diligence Questionnaire, with a worksheet linking relevant questions to assessment categories. ILPA provides no standard numerical scores because priorities differ; LPs may create weighted, directional scores to guide dialogue. Suggested resources include ILPA materials, UNPRI, SASB, TCFD, and IIGCC. ILPA welcomes feedback at esg@ilpa.org and may update the Framework, which LPs can adapt to their own policies.
